sections.heading: Why blood pressure matters
sections.content: High blood pressure often has no symptoms, but it can raise the risk of heart disease, stroke, kidney disease, and other complications. Regular measurement is important because symptoms alone are unreliable.

sections.heading: Healthy habits
sections.content: Common prevention and management habits include eating a heart-healthy diet, reducing sodium, staying physically active, limiting alcohol, avoiding tobacco, sleeping enough, and taking prescribed medicines as directed.

sections.heading: When to get care
sections.content: Very high readings, chest pain, shortness of breath, severe headache, weakness, confusion, or vision changes can signal urgent or emergency problems. Users should seek immediate medical care for emergency symptoms.
